labeling_rules: Draft direct-implementation evidence for narrow mechanisms. For whole-function questions include all fragments of that function; for a narrow branch include the containing fragment. Documentation/imports/call sites are not exhaustively labeled. Await learner review before scoring or making quality claims.
limitations: Three Codex-authored development cases; relevance judgments are drafts, not independent human labels.
No held-out independence: source and related identifier diagnostics have already been inspected.
Labels select direct implementation evidence, not every potentially useful explanatory chunk; recall is relative to these narrow labels only.
All cases are supported; unsupported behavior and broader task coverage are not represented.
Source export is GitContext commit 548076ad03eb936c61b8d7540feb65d5da8f60e2. Local export has no own Git repository; ancestor rejection is recorded as root_is_subdirectory.
Runtime/chunking configuration is fixed in the snapshot; a different snapshot or parser/policy requires revalidation.
Review and scoring are separate. No evaluation run, quality score, latency report, or formal ten-question set is supplied.

cases.question: Where does GitContext write a snapshot to a temporary file, verify it, and atomically replace the saved snapshot?
How does GitContext decide whether a saved snapshot is current, stale, or unknown?
What prevents CLI search from returning ranked snippets when source freshness is stale or unknown?
